newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers mostly steady.

text.p: Rail and truck soymeal offers were mostly steady on Thursday and movement was spotty as most end-users waited for the October contract to expire, several cash brokers said.
"I don't know why people would be buying the October when they could wait until Monday or Tuesday and buy versus the December," a Kentucky broker said.

He was referring to an $8.80 premium CBOT October held over December soymeal prices. He said end-users had been sidelined since September by high prices but some were starting to run out of supplies and were eager to buy.
"They were able to live hand to mouth in September and continued to do so as we got through October," he said. "Now they don't have the pipeline to back them up."
Soybean supplies continued to be tight as producers were reluctant to sell, several brokers noted.
"Bean buying is still difficult," an Indiana dealer said. "There hasn't been that much movement."
Some dealers continued to report high moisture levels but most said soybeans were starting to dry down.
"We're noticing that the moisture is coming down," another Indiana dealer said. "We just wish the beans would come in."
